visual_confirmation.note: Rendered and visually inspected BEFORE trusting the RAM-divergence heuristic alone (per the wave-4 false-positive-mint lessons). Stage 1 factory-rooftop gameplay confirmed: lives HUD ('L-' + heart icons), score HUD ('000000'), ladders/crane background, and a visibly displaced/turned player sprite comparing the RIGHT-90 render against the NOOP-90 render from the same state. Not a title screen, directional cursor, or text-advance screen.

odometer_gate.note: Real, non-flat x-axis under held RIGHT with full OAM churn (agent clearly active/animating every step) -- no need to invoke the possible-asm-cpu-anomaly cross-check (that check applies only when the trace comes back completely flat under every direction; this one did not).

smoke.note: The tool itself raised 'STALL WARNING: stuck at 16 cells for 2 min straight -- possible frozen/dead state' (stall_flat_windows=2, c_local_delta=0). Growth happened in minute 1 (1->16) then completely froze in minute 2 with the frontier fully closed (0 open cells) -- this is the exact shape wave 4 classified Mega Man as SOUND_GAME_STOPS on (frozen at 10 cells in minute 2 despite a real 72px x-axis), not the Super C shape (which still ticked +1 cell in minute 2). The x-axis here is real and larger (245px, full OAM churn) so this is not a camera-static / dead-agent finding.

classification_rationale: Odometer gate confirms a real, non-flat x-axis (245px range, 1199/1199 OAM churn -- agent unambiguously alive and animating). The 2-minute/4-worker smoke grew the archive from 1 to 16 cells in minute 1, then went completely flat (byte-identical cells/frontier/best_score) through minute 2, triggering the harness's own built-in stall warning. Frozen frontier despite a real, confirmed axis is the SOUND_GAME_STOPS shape, not SOUND_ADVANCING (which requires growth to continue, however slowly, through the budget) and not CAMERA_STATIC_AGENT_ACTIVE (there is a real axis here).
next_lever: The discovered lives byte (0x0051) reads 0 at the start state -- flagged, not confirmed, same pattern as Mega Man's wave-4 lead. If that is not literally 'lives remaining,' a decrement on the first hit could underflow toward 255 and read as an unrecoverable death, killing every worker at the same early obstacle and starving the frontier at 16 cells / gx 53. Re-running discover_observables against a slightly-advanced (post-first-hazard) state, or instrumenting a raw per-step lives/death trace during a short solver burst, would confirm or rule this out before committing more compute.
wall_clock_budget: workers capped at 4, smoke capped at 2 minutes per task instructions (shared machine, concurrent v28 training + an ASM-CPU investigation workflow both running).
